subject: Extension of the JS Model as a multistate model with multiple states

messages.author: d63f1fcb60ee8a1c
messages.subject: Extension of the JS Model as a multistate model with multiple states
parts:
Dear all,

Foreword: This is my first post, so please forgive me if my question is inappropriate for this list, let me know and I will adjust.


I have adapted the code in chapter 10 of the Kéry and Schaub book that fits the JS model as a multistate model but instead of having just 3 states: not yet entered, alive and dead, I have 3 additional alive states so in total 5: not yet entered, breeders, non-breeder, juveniles and dead. I have changed the state transition matrix and the observation matrix accordingly. The main change is that instead of having only one entry probability (gamma), I have one entry probability per alive state. My code runs properly on a simplified subset of my data. However I would like to be sure that I am correctly implementing the changes to the prior and the calculation of the population parameters. If someone could have a look at my model below, I would be very grateful. I have not shared a dataset, however, if you want one to play around with the model, I can provide one. 

Many thanks!

Tina



 model {
    
    #--------------------------------------
    # Parameters:
    # phi: survival probability
    # gamma: removal entry probability
    # p: capture probability
    #--------------------------------------
    # States (S):
    # 1 not yet entered
    # 2 Breeder
    # 3 Non breeder
    # 4 Juvenile
    # 5 dead
    # Observations (O):
    # 1 seen as breeder 
    # 2 seen as non-breeder
    # 3 seen as juvenile
    # 4 not seen
    #--------------------------------------
    
    # Priors and constraints
    for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
    
    phiB[t] <- mean.phi.1
    phiNB[t]<- mean.phi.2
    phiJ[t] <- mean.phi.3
    
    psiBNB[t] <- mean.psi.1
    psiNBB[t]<- mean.psi.2
    
    
    pB[t] <- mean.p.1
    pNB[t] <- mean.p.2
    pJ[t]<- mean.p.3

    #dirichlet dist to make sure that all the gammas (+1) sum to one.
for (k in 1:4){
beta[k, t] ~ dgamma(1, 1)
gamma[k, t]<-beta[k,t]/sum(beta[,t])

}    

    }

    mean.phi.1 ~ dunif(0, 1)  
    mean.phi.2 ~ dunif(0, 1)  
    mean.phi.3 ~ dunif(0, 1)
    
    mean.psi.1 ~ dunif(0, 1)
    mean.psi.2 ~ dunif(0, 1)
    
    
    mean.p.1 ~ dunif(0, 1)    
    mean.p.2 ~ dunif(0, 1)   
    mean.p.3 ~ dunif(0, 1)
    
    
    
    # Define state-transition and observation matrices   
    for (i in 1:M){  
    # Define probabilities of state S(t+1) given S(t)
    for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
    ps[1,i,t,1]<- 1 - (gamma[1,t] + gamma[2,t] + gamma[3,t])
    ps[1,i,t,2]<- gamma[1,t]
    ps[1,i,t,3]<- gamma[2,t]
    ps[1,i,t,4]<- gamma[3,t]
    ps[1,i,t,5]<- 0
    
    ps[2,i,t,1] <- 0
    ps[2,i,t,2] <- phiB[t] * (1-psiBNB[t])
    ps[2,i,t,3] <- phiB[t] * psiBNB[t]
    ps[2,i,t,4] <- 0
    ps[2,i,t,5] <- 1-phiB[t]

    ps[3,i,t,1] <- 0
    ps[3,i,t,2] <- phiNB[t] * psiNBB[t]
    ps[3,i,t,3] <- phiNB[t] * (1-psiNBB[t])
    ps[3,i,t,4] <- 0
    ps[3,i,t,5] <- 1-phiNB[t]
    
    ps[4,i,t,1] <- 0    
    ps[4,i,t,2] <- 0
    ps[4,i,t,3] <- phiJ[t]
    ps[4,i,t,4] <- 0
    ps[4,i,t,5] <- 1- phiJ[t]
    
    ps[5,i,t,1] <- 0   
    ps[5,i,t,2] <- 0
    ps[5,i,t,3] <- 0
    ps[5,i,t,4] <- 0
    ps[5,i,t,5] <- 1 

    
    # Define probabilities of O(t) given S(t)
    po[1,i,t,1] <- 0
    po[1,i,t,2] <- 0
    po[1,i,t,3] <- 0
    po[1,i,t,4] <- 1


    po[2,i,t,1] <- pB[t]
    po[2,i,t,2] <- 0
    po[2,i,t,3] <- 0
    po[2,i,t,4] <- 1-pB[t]

    po[3,i,t,1] <- pNB[t]
    po[3,i,t,2] <- 0
    po[3,i,t,3] <- 0
    po[3,i,t,4] <- 1-pNB[t]

    po[4,i,t,1] <- pJ[t]
    po[4,i,t,2] <- 0
    po[4,i,t,3] <- 0
    po[4,i,t,4] <- 1-pJ[t]

    po[5,i,t,1] <- 0
    po[5,i,t,2] <- 0
    po[5,i,t,3] <- 0
    po[5,i,t,4] <- 1
    } #t
    } #i
    
    # Likelihood 
    for (i in 1:M){
    # Define latent state at first occasion
    z[i,1] <- 1   # Make sure that all M individuals are in state 1 at t=1
    for (t in 2:n.occasions){
    # State process: draw S(t) given S(t-1)
    z[i,t] ~ dcat(ps[z[i,t-1], i, t-1,])

    # Observation process: draw O(t) given S(t)
    y[i,t] ~ dcat(po[z[i,t], i, t-1,])
    } #t
    } #i
    
    # Calculate derived population parameters
    for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
    qgamma[t] <- 1-gamma[1,t]-gamma[2,t]-gamma[3,t]
    }
    cprob[1] <- gamma[1,1]+gamma[2,1]+gamma[3,1]
    for (t in 2:(n.occasions-1)){
    cprob[t] <- (gamma[1,t]-gamma[2,t]-gamma[3,t]) * prod(qgamma[1:(t-1)])
    } #t
    psi <- sum(cprob[])            # Inclusion probability
    for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
    b[t] <- cprob[t] / psi      # Entry probability
    } #t
    
    for (i in 1:M){
    for (t in 2:n.occasions){
    Bal[i,t-1] <- equals(z[i,t], 2)
    NBal[i,t-1] <- equals(z[i,t], 3)
    Jal[i,t-1] <- equals(z[i,t], 4)
    } #t
    for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
    d[i,t] <- equals(z[i,t]-Bal[i,t]- NBal[i,t]-Jal[i,t],0)
    } #t   
    Balive[i] <- sum(Bal[i,])
    NBalive[i] <- sum(NBal[i,])
    Jalive[i] <- sum(Jal[i,])
    alive[i]<- sum(Bal[i,])+sum(NBal[i,])+sum(Jal[i,])
    } #i
    
    for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
    N[t] <- sum(Bal[,t])+sum(NBal[,t])+sum(Jal[,t])     # Actual population size
    B[t] <- sum(d[,t])         # Number of entries
    } #t
    for (i in 1:M){
    w[i] <- 1-equals(alive[i],0)
    } #i
    Nsuper <- sum(w[])            # Superpopulation size
    }

messages.subject: Re: Extension of the JS Model as a multistate model with multiple states
parts:
Hi Tina, sometimes it is helpful to have additional comments in the code for the multistate probabilities to keep things obvious.  For example:

#po[true,i,t,obs]

This indicates the location of the true latent state index vs. the observed state index.  I think you have a couple errors in the observed states:

This is saying that the probability of observing state 1 (seen as breeder) when the true state is 3 (non-breeder) is pNB[t].  That probability should be zero, no?  You should never be observing a nonbreeder as a breeder, unless there is state miss-classification error.  I think pNB[t] should be located at po[3,i,t,2].  The same goes for the pJ[t] probability, which should be at po[4,i,t,3].
